new_task_1.title: Expose decode_complete in the top-level jwt package API
new_task_1.description: PyJWT 2.10.0 adds `decode_complete` to the symbols re-exported from `jwt.__init__` and to `__all__`, making it available directly as `jwt.decode_complete` and via `from jwt import decode_complete` without importing from internal submodules.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the `decode_complete` helper is part of the public top-level `jwt` package API so callers can access it directly from `jwt` without reaching into `jwt.api_jwt`.

expectation.grounded: The package initializer should import `decode_complete` from `jwt.api_jwt` and include it in `__all__`. After the upgrade, `import jwt; jwt.decode_complete(...)` and `from jwt import decode_complete` should both resolve successfully.
expectation.conceptual: The full decode API should be consistently exposed at the package root alongside `decode` and `encode`, reducing the need for users to depend on internal module paths.

constraints.grounded: Existing top-level exports such as `decode` and `encode` must remain unchanged. This change is an API-surface addition only; it does not by itself alter the behavior or signature of `decode_complete`.
constraints.conceptual: The update should improve discoverability and import ergonomics without breaking existing imports or changing decode semantics.

behavior: `jwt.decode_complete` is now available as a top-level attribute on the package
`from jwt import decode_complete` now succeeds without importing from `jwt.api_jwt`
`decode_complete` is included in the package's declared public exports via `__all__`
acceptance_criteria: When a user imports `jwt`, the module exposes a `decode_complete` attribute
When a user runs `from jwt import decode_complete`, the import succeeds
Existing top-level imports such as `from jwt import decode, encode` continue to work unchanged
Calling the top-level `jwt.decode_complete` function behaves the same as calling `jwt.api_jwt.decode_complete`
